findings.summary: the noteless-fallback test could not fail: at budget 200 the untruncatable head means zero lines are packed, so the restore loop never runs — three independent gut-jobs of that branch each left all 12 tests green. Rewritten at budget 395 (the restore band); all three mutations now observed RED, and it additionally asserts the restored line ORDER, since the pop-out/pop-back pattern is a double stack reversal.
required check review-gate was red — an implementation change (src/export.ts) carried no reviews/<sha>.json record (ADR-0052). This record closes it.

'guaranteed fit' was stated absolutely, but the head is untruncatable: a budget-sweep (100..4000 step 37, five entry-size mixes) found overshoot at exactly the budgets below the head length and nowhere else. Comment now scopes the contract to budgets exceeding the never-dropped head — the same scope renderContextBundle's fixedLen() carries — and states that units are UTF-16 code units, not bytes.

the digit-width re-check is the loop's stated justification and no test crosses a 9->10 or 99->100 boundary; convergence was verified by analysis and by the sweep (each eviction removes >=10 chars while the note grows by at most 1), so this is a coverage gap rather than a defect.

just above the head+note boundary the loop can evict every knowledge line to make room for a note about them, yielding a note-only export. Same tradeoff the parity target (renderContextBundle) makes, and unreachable from the CLI since runExport exposes no --budget.
